title: Allah holds believers steady with the firm word.
subtitle: Steady here, and steady in the grave
then: After the parable of the two trees, this verse says Allah keeps believers firm with that good word. Ibn Kathir cites Bukhari: {reward}when the Muslim is questioned in the grave, he testifies La ilaha illallah and that Muhammad ﷺ is Allah's Messenger.{/reward} {idea}That is the firm word.{/idea}
now: The doctor's face changes as she reads the results. Your hands go cold. What comes out of your mouth in that moment is what you have practised. {reward}Allah steadies the tongue that has said His name often.{/reward}
old: I will find the right words when the hard moment comes.
new: The word I repeat now is the one Allah makes firm for me later.
try: Ask Allah today: O Allah, keep me firm with the firm word in this life and the next.

title: They traded Allah's blessing for ingratitude.
subtitle: Swapping a gift for its opposite
then: Ibn Abbas said this refers to the people of Makkah. Ali said {reward}the blessing was faith, which came to the leaders of Quraysh{/reward}, and they {trap}exchanged it for disbelief and led their people to ruin{/trap}. Ibn Kathir adds the Prophet ﷺ was sent as a blessing to all mankind.
now: You were raised hearing the Quran at home, and now it sits unopened. The masjid is a five-minute walk and you have not been in months. {reward}Faith within reach is a blessing.{/reward} Leaders of a home lead others too.
old: Being born near faith is just background.
new: Faith within reach is a blessing I can either keep or trade away.
try: Use one blessing of faith near you today: the nearby masjid, the Quran on your shelf.

title: A wretched place to settle.
subtitle: Where the trade ends
then: The verse names the home of ruin that the leaders led their people into. {trap}It is Hell, a wretched place to settle.{/trap} It is stated briefly and soberly, a warning to people in Makkah who still had time to choose.
now: You plan where you will live, which school, which neighbourhood, for years ahead. {idea}The last home is the one that matters most.{/idea} The choices that lead there are made in ordinary days like this one.
old: I will think about the final home much later.
new: Where I end up is shaped by the small choices I make today.
try: Make the dua today: O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and seek refuge with You from the Fire.

title: Enjoy for now, but the destination is set.
subtitle: Rivals to Allah, and a brief enjoyment
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}set up partners to Allah and called people to worship them{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ is told to say: enjoy yourselves. It is a warning, not permission. He links it to: {idea}We let them enjoy a little, then they return to Us.{/idea}
now: The weekend plan, the new car, the trip. None of it is wrong. But if it all quietly becomes the point of life, {idea}enjoyment turns into a rival{/idea}. Enjoy, and remember where you are heading.
old: Enjoying life now is all that really counts.
new: Enjoyment is brief; what I put in Allah's place decides my end.
try: Notice one pleasure today that you lean on too much, and thank Allah for it out loud.

title: Pray and give now, before a Day with no deals.
subtitle: A message to My servants who believe
then: After the warning, a gentle turn: {idea}tell My servants who believe{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says pray on time with humility, and spend on relatives and others. Qatadah said friendships made for Allah last; {trap}others will be cut off{/trap}. On that Day no ransom or bargain is accepted.
now: You know the right people, you can negotiate any deal, you have a cousin in every office. {idea}None of that works on that Day.{/idea} What works is the two rakahs you prayed and the money you quietly gave.
old: My network and my bargaining will always get me through.
new: Prayer and giving now are what count on the Day of no deals.
try: Give a small charity today in secret, and pray your next prayer on time.

title: Rain, fruit, ships and rivers, all put to your service.
subtitle: Look at what you use every day
then: Right after telling believers to pray and give, the verse reminds them who provides. Ibn Kathir lists {reward}rain bringing fruits of many colours and tastes, seas that carry ships between lands, rivers for drinking and farming{/reward}. {idea}It is Allah who made all of it serve people.{/idea}
now: The banana on your breakfast table crossed an ocean in a container ship. The tap water came from a river you have never seen. {reward}Every bite and sip passed through His favour.{/reward}
old: Supermarkets and pipes just work; there is nothing to notice.
new: Everything that feeds me runs by Allah's command.
try: At your next meal, think of one step that brought the food to you, and say Alhamdulillah.

title: Sun, moon, night and day run on schedule for you.
subtitle: The clock you never wound
then: The list of favours continues into the sky. Ibn Kathir says {reward}the sun and moon keep their courses{/reward}, and night and day each lengthen and shorten in turn. He links it to: the sun does not overtake the moon, {idea}each floats in its orbit{/idea}.
now: Your alarm goes off at six because you trust the sun will rise. You plan Ramadan by a moon you never moved. {reward}Your whole calendar rests on His favour.{/reward}
old: Sunrise and sunset are just how things are.
new: The sun, moon, night and day were set running for me by Allah.
try: Watch the sunset or sunrise today for one minute and remember who set it running.

title: Try to count His blessings and you will fail.
subtitle: Given more than asked, and still ungrateful
then: After the list, the conclusion: {reward}if you count Allah's favours, you could never finish{/reward}. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet's ﷺ dua: All praise is Yours, never enough. He reports Dawud asked: {idea}how can I thank You, when my thanks is also Your favour?{/idea}
now: You spend twenty minutes listing what is wrong in your life to a friend. Try listing what is right and you stop at breath, eyesight, one person who loves you, and realise {reward}the list has no end{/reward}.
old: I have a good idea of what Allah has given me.
new: His favours outnumber my counting, so gratitude never finishes.
try: Set a timer for two minutes and list blessings out loud without stopping.

title: Ibrahim asked for a safe city and a protected family.
subtitle: The founder of Makkah prays
then: Ibn Kathir says this was said to the idol worshippers of Makkah: {idea}the House was built on worship of Allah alone{/idea}, and its founder Ibrahim prayed against idols. Allah accepted his dua for safety. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}a person praying should also ask for their parents and children{/reward}.
now: You pray quickly for your exam, your job, your health. Ibrahim prayed for the city and his sons, and for their faith most of all. {reward}Add your children and your home to your dua.{/reward}
old: My dua is mostly about my own needs.
new: Like Ibrahim, I pray for my family's faith and my home's safety too.
try: Tonight add one line to your dua: O Allah, keep me and my children far from worshipping other than You.

title: Whoever disobeys me, You are still Forgiving, Merciful.
subtitle: Ibrahim leaves the stubborn to Allah's mercy
then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim disowned idol worship but {reward}left those who disobeyed to Allah{/reward}, like Isa's words: if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise. He reports that {idea}the Prophet ﷺ recited both, raised his hands, and said: O Allah, my Ummah, my Ummah.{/idea}
now: A sibling has walked away from the deen, and part of you wants to write them off. Ibrahim's words show another way. {reward}Leave them to the Forgiving, the Merciful, and keep praying.{/reward}
old: Those who reject the truth deserve to be written off.
new: I can stand by the truth and still leave people to Allah's mercy.
try: Make dua tonight, by name, for someone who has turned away from faith.

title: A barren valley, chosen so they would pray.
subtitle: Ibrahim's family by the Sacred House
then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim made this dua after the House was built. He settled family in a valley with no crops {idea}so they could establish prayer{/idea}. He asked that {reward}hearts incline to them and fruits reach them{/reward}. Allah answered: fruit of every kind is brought to Makkah, though none grows there.
now: You are choosing where to live: the bigger flat far from any masjid, or the smaller one near. Ibrahim chose by one question. {idea}Where will my family be able to pray?{/idea} Provision followed.
old: I choose where to live by comfort and price.
new: Like Ibrahim, I can choose for prayer first and trust Allah for provision.
try: Ask yourself one honest question: what in my home helps my family pray? Improve one thing.

title: You know what we hide and what we show.
subtitle: Ibrahim's sincerity before his Lord

row.title: Allah
sub: nothing hidden in earth or sky

then: Ibn Jarir explains Ibrahim meant: {idea}You know the intention behind my dua for this town, that I seek Your pleasure sincerely.{/idea} He left his family in a barren valley. {reward}Allah knew exactly why.{/reward}
now: You made a hard decision: moved away, left a job, said no to a family plan. People misread it. {reward}Allah knows what you meant.{/reward} You do not have to win every explanation.
old: If people misunderstand my intentions, I have failed.
new: Allah knows what I hide and what I show; that is enough.
try: Before one action today, set your intention privately for Allah alone.

title: Children in old age: my Lord hears every dua.
subtitle: Ibrahim thanks Allah for Isma'il and Ishaq
then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {reward}praised Allah for giving him children after he had grown old{/reward}. He notes Isma'il was thirteen years older than Ishaq. Ibrahim's lesson: {idea}He accepts the dua of those who call on Him.{/idea}
now: You have been asking for something for years: a child, a spouse, healing, a way out of debt. People hint it is too late. {idea}Ibrahim was answered in old age.{/idea} Keep asking, and praise Him for what has already come.
old: If it has not happened by now, it never will.
new: My Lord hears every dua, and His timing has no age limit.
try: Begin your next dua with praise for one answered prayer, then ask again.
